newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH UNION, EMPLOYER EMU VIEWS DUE MAY/JUNE - TT.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH UNION, EMPLOYER EMU VIEWS DUE MAY/JUNE - TT.

text.p: Central trade unions and employer confederations are due to work out by late May or early June a joint resolution on the effects on the labour markets of Finnish membership of EMU, a big employer group said on Monday.
"Exploratory talks have not brought up any major problem," director-general Johannes Koroma of the Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT) told Reuters.
"We have established a target to make it (the resolution) public by the end of May or early in June," he said, speaking on the sidelines of a seminar arranged by TT.
"The only remaining big question is the timing," he said.
Asked about the contents of the resolution, Koroma said: "It will examine the factors of EMU which affect the labour markets." He did not elaborate.

Big trade unions have called for a joint union-employer resolution on EMU, aiming for assurances that the Finnish collective bargaining system will not be abolished if Finland joins European ecnomic and monetary union.
Unions have also called for so called buffer funds to protect wages and jobs in a cyclical downturn. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
